title: Why the Same Import Surge Reaches Towns Differently — Timothy Bartik’s (1991) Shift-Share Instruments, Autor–Dorn–Hanson Local Labor-Market China Trade Exposure & Borusyak–Hull–Jaravel Shock Orthogonality

teenKit.tldr: In 15 seconds: When national trade or industry booms and busts hit the country, why do neighboring towns feel totally different shocks? Bartik's shift-share instrument multiplies each town's historic factory mix by national industry shifts—and modern econometrics reveals which assumption actually makes that causal.
teenKit.whyItMatters: Policymakers can't run randomized trials on national trade surges, so shift-share math is one of economics' most important tools for measuring real-world job impacts.
keyTakeaways: A Bartik (shift-share) measure weights national or foreign industry shocks ('shifts') by a local region's pre-existing employment shares ('shares').
Autor, Dorn, and Hanson (2013) used Chinese exports to other high-income countries paired with earlier U.S. commuting-zone factory shares to isolate supply-driven import competition.
Goldsmith-Pinkham, Sorkin & Swift vs. Borusyak, Hull & Jaravel clarified two distinct paths to validity: exogenous local shares vs. many quasi-random industry shocks.

vocab.meaning: An exposure index summing (local initial industry share x national/external industry shock) across sectors.
A cluster of counties grouped by journey-to-work flows to represent a self-contained local labor market.
When local economic booms or slumps change imports directly, confounding naive correlations.

quiz.question: Why did Autor, Dorn, and Hanson instrument U.S. imports from China using Chinese export growth to eight other high-income nations?
options: Because U.S. customs lost its records
To isolate China's internal productivity/supply surge from U.S.-specific domestic demand shocks
Because commuting zones have identical factory shares
quiz.explanation: Exports rising simultaneously across other high-income countries capture China's supply shock rather than local U.S. demand shifts.
